thread:
samir: FYI ap-southeast warm pool failing ~30% of node inits since 03:40 UTC, suspecting KMS decrypt errors on model keys.
leo: saw alerts too. `apac.gpu.pool.init.fail` spiked. I pulled a node log: `ERROR: kms:DecryptAccessDenied Key=arn:aws:kms:ap-southeast-1:1111:key/abcd-1234`
maria: we rolled the egress lockdown rules last deploy for audit-hardening (fw-group: edge-egress-tighten-2026). Did we accidentally remove keystore endpoint CIDR?
samir: logs show attempts to reach keystore at 10.4.12.34:443 and getting RST. Correlation with deploy-bot message at 03:35: `applied firewall policy edge-egress-tighten-2026`
deploy-bot: firewall update applied to sg-rt-ap-southeast (removed outbound 0.0.0.0/0:443 allow).
esther: Oof — we scoped the allow too narrowly. We expected the keystore to be on privatelink, but the keystore is still on an internal ENI range.
oncall-sre: creating incident runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/gpu-keystore-egress
leo: quick mitigation options: 1) temporary allow egress to 10.4.12.34/32:443 from warm pool SG; 2) create VPC endpoint for keystore (longer but durable); 3) fall back to local cached keys (not supported currently). Which do we want?
maria: short-term = option 1. I'll scope to ENI-IP and warm-pool SG only. We'll follow up with endpoint in a tracked RFC.
samir: agree. Also need to evaluate cost: keep in mind cross-az egress to keystore ENIs may add small data charges when scaled. Note gatekeeper metrics: "expected monthly delta < $500" if temporary.
opsbot: alert suppressed for 15m by samir.
leo: adding rule now: `aws ec2 authorize-security-group-egress --group-id sg-warmpool --protocol tcp --port 443 --cidr 10.4.12.34/32 --description "temp allow to keystore after fw tighten"`
leo: done — nodes are starting to come up again, failure rate dropping from 30% -> 5% in last 5m.
maria: opening PR to add VPC endpoint + IAM policy that restricts key usage from that endpoint; linking in infra board. PR: https://github.com/redwood-infra/policies/pull/182
esther: also adding a short-term audit entry for change window and who approved (compliance needs this).
oncall-sre: reminder: run an eval to ensure no key material persisted on nodes. If leak risk is non-zero we need a rotate.
samir: good point. We'll schedule a key rotation with a canary rollout after endpoint is in place.
maria: postmortem / followup items: 1) tighten deploy gating so egress lockdowns check for known internal endpoints; 2) add e2e before/after for keystore ENI reachability in the warm pool job; 3) estimate monthly cost of VPC endpoint and add to spreadsheet.
leo: closing the incident if metrics hold for 30m. Thanks all :thumbsup:
